title: DPA addendum — On-prem evidence handback & audit procedure (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a draft addendum intended to sit alongside the standard Redwood DPA for customers deploying Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) that require formalized evidence handback, forensic snapshot, and audit access procedures. It is intended for high-risk regulated customers who need contractual guarantees around: timely delivery of evidence, cryptographic key handling (BYOK), chain-of-custody for forensic artifacts, and an agreed-upon timeline for triangular investigation support (customer, Redwood, subprocessor).

Scope & applicability:
Applies only when the customer selects the 'On-Prem Evidence & Audit Addendum' in the private deployment SOW. Covers: access to logs, forensic snapshots, delivery of cryptographic evidence, proof-of-deletion certificates, and onsite/remote audit coordination. Does NOT change general DPA obligations on data processing, but augments them with operational commitments specific to on-prem/private deployments.

Key definitions (for negotiation clarity):
- "Forensic Snapshot": a point-in-time copy of runtime memory dump(s), relevant log files (application, system, orchestration), and metadata (container IDs, host identifiers) produced according to the Snapshot Procedure in Section 4.
- "Evidence Bundle": compiled artifacts delivered to the customer or to an independent auditor consisting of Forensic Snapshots, correlated logs, and chain-of-custody records.
- "Proof of Deletion Certificate": Redwood-issued signed statement and associated deletion logs confirming removal of specified data from Redwood-managed components.

Customer Audit Rights (high level):
1) Remote review: Customer (or an agreed independent auditor) may request a remote evidence bundle within the timelines and scope in Section 4.
2) Onsite inspections: Where the deployment is physically hosted by the customer, Redwood staff may be required to assist in person. Conversely, where Redwood-hosted infrastructure is used in a dedicated manner, onsite visits by the customer's auditor are limited to the scope in the SOW and require 30 days notice.
3) Frequency: Default allowed audit frequency is once per 12 months; additional audits permitted for cause (breach, regulatory request), subject to mutual agreement on scope and cost.

Forensic Snapshot & Evidence Handback Procedure (operational draft):
- Triggering events: security incident declared by either party, regulator request, or agreed audit window.
- Request channel: formal request via security@redwood.com and referencing SOW and ticket created in SEC-7421.
- Acceptance & scheduling: Redwood acknowledges within 48 hours, provides an estimated delivery plan within 5 business days.
- Data minimization: Redwood will scope the snapshot to the minimum set of artifacts necessary to address the request.
- Snapshot capture: performed by Redwood engineers or by the customer under Redwood supervision (if customer-held infra). Capture steps include: block-level snapshot of relevant hosts (if available), export of container logs since T-72 hours, KV cache metadata export, and process lists.
- Chain of custody: every snapshot will be digitally signed (pgp/ed25519) by the capturing engineer and logged; hashes of each artifact will be recorded and shared with the customer.
- Evidence bundle delivery: encrypted transfer (customer-provided SFTP endpoint or PGP/email-of-record) within 10 business days for routine audit requests, 3 business days for incident response escalations. Delays and scope extensions will be communicated with reasons.

BYOK, Key Escrow & Cryptographic Evidence:
- BYOK stance: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for storage and transport of sensitive artifacts. If customer elects BYOK, Redwood will deliver evidence encrypted under the customer key material and will not retain unencrypted copies longer than required for operations and incident response (default 7 days unless otherwise negotiated).
- Escrow: where regulatory regimes require escrow, Redwood will use mutually agreeable escrow agents; escrow process must be added to SOW.
- Key evidence: logs that include KMS audit events, envelope-wrapping metadata, and key IDs will be included in evidence bundles where relevant. Redwood will not disclose key material itself.

Proof of Deletion & Retention Certificates:
- After remediation actions, customer may request a Proof of Deletion Certificate for specific artifacts. Redwood will produce a signed certificate containing: scope of deletion, deletion method, timestamp(s), operator ID(s), and deletion logs (where system-retained).
- Certificate delivery timeline: within 10 business days of validated deletion.

Service levels & costs (negotiable):
- Evidence delivery SLA (standard audit): 10 business days.
- Evidence delivery SLA (security incident): 3 business days initial package, followed by a complete bundle within 10 business days.
- Onsite auditor support: Redwood staff time billed at professional services rates for >8 hours support per audit. Routine audits limited to 2 staff-days unless otherwise agreed.

Roles & responsibilities (operational matrix — narrative):
- Customer: provide precise scope, endpoints for evidence transfer, any required key material (for BYOK), and a point of contact (SOC/Legal).
- Redwood: capture and deliver artifacts as scoped; maintain chain-of-custody logs; coordinate with subprocessors; redact third-party customer data where appropriate; ensure evidence confidentiality.
- Independent auditor (if used): operate under NDA, agreed scope, and return/destroy obligations mirroring those in this addendum.

Confidentiality, data minimization & redaction:
All evidence is subject to the DPA confidentiality provisions. Redwood may redact information that contains unrelated third-party customer data but will provide a redaction log describing what was removed and rationale.

Escalation & regulatory notifications:
- Redwood will notify the customer within 24 hours of becoming aware of any incident that may require evidence requests under this addendum.
- For regulator-driven requests, Redwood will cooperate and share only the scope of artifacts legally required unless otherwise authorized by customer.

Negotiation notes / open items (items to push back on or confirm):
- Onsite audit frequency cap (we want once per 12 months; customers may ask for once per 6 months).
- Evidence delivery timelines for enterprise customers with large volumes (may require longer due to export complexity).
- Cost model for repeated forensics (proposal: first two incidents per 12 months included; excess on time-and-materials).
- Language around Redwood’s ability to redact or withhold proprietary operational details that would materially harm Redwood’s service if disclosed. Suggest a carve-out with predefined redaction categories.

Suggested draft clause (to be stitched into DPA as Annex X):
"Annex X — On-Prem Evidence Handback and Audit Procedure
1. Definitions: [as above]
2. Audit Rights: Customer may request evidence as set out in this Annex; Redwood will comply subject to the timelines and limitations herein.
3. Evidence Capture: Redwood shall capture, sign, and deliver Evidence Bundles in accordance with the Forensic Snapshot Procedure.
4. Delivery: Evidence Bundles shall be provided via encrypted transfer to Customer endpoints within the timelines herein.
5. Confidentiality: All Evidence Bundles are Customer Confidential Information and are subject to the DPA's confidentiality obligations.
6. Costs: Redwood may invoice reasonable costs for excessive or non-routine audits as described in the SOW.
7. Dispute & Escalation: Parties will follow the escalation path in the Master Agreement; any unresolved dispute regarding scope will be submitted to senior security representatives for mediation prior to other remedies."

Appendix A — Capture checklist (operational template):
- Request ID and scope
- Time window (T0, T-72h)
- Hosts/containers included
- Logs: systemd, application, orchestration, network flow (if available)
- Memory dump(s) included (Y/N) and tool used
- Hashes recorded and signed
- Transfer mechanism specified

References & related artifacts:
- Internal SEC-7421 ticket (captures incident & audit coordination notes)
notes: Working draft for legal/security review. Priya to circulate to Sales AE for SOW implications and to Legal for redlines. Aim to produce a v1.0 (customer-facing) by end of Q2 2026.
